name: Hall in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Historic old town featuring the famous Haller Münzturm and one of the best-preserved city centers in Tirol.
beschreibung:
Hall in Tirol lies at 574 m above sea level, only about ten kilometers east of Innsbruck on the right bank of the Inn, and with around 13,900 inhabitants it forms one of the historically most significant towns in the state. The name refers to the medieval salt ("hall" = salt-bearing), which was traded and processed here over centuries. Together with Innsbruck, Hall shares the rank as a center of the Innsbruck region, but as an independent town with its own district of Innsbruck-Land it retains a clearly defined character.

The heart of the town is one of the best-preserved old town centers of Tirol, with winding alleys, late Gothic burgher houses, and the famous Münzturm, which rises above the roofs and is visible from afar. The tower, built in 1505, was part of the mint where the famous "Haller Thaler" was minted between 1477 and 1766 – once one of the most important means of payment of the Habsburg Empire. Today the tower houses the Museum „Münzturm" and provides insight into the history of mining in Tirol. Other sights include the late Gothic parish church of St. Nikolaus with its 78-meter-high tower, the town hall from the 14th century, and Burg Hasegg, which houses the town museum. The Oberer Stadtplatz with its arcades and cafés invites you to linger.

In addition to culture and history, Hall offers a surprisingly lively shopping mile: Rosengasse and Unterer Stadtplatz have established themselves as popular shopping destinations that can compete with Innsbruck's city center. Culinary offerings range from the traditional Tyrolean inn with Kasnocken and Tiroler Gröstl to cozy cafés in historic walls. Anyone who visits Hall gets a compact, honest Tyrolean
